Stated Claim / Post Context:
ICE raids home of Democratic US congresswoman Ilhan Omar

Democrats accuse Donald Trump of "abusing his power" as immigration agents carry out a pre-dawn raid on the home of Ilhan Omar, a naturalised US citizen born in Somalia.

Actual Article Body:
Emergency

TOK PISIN

Topic:World Politics

Ilhan Omar is a longtime and vocal critic of Donald Trump's administration. (Reuters: Tim Evans)

Democrats in the US have accused President Donald Trump of "abusing his power" after immigration agents carried out a pre-dawn raid on the home of Ilhan Omar, a naturalised US citizen born in Somalia.

Ms Omar, who represents a seat in the US state of Minnesota, has been a frequent target of Mr Trump in recent years.

The raid comes just over three weeks out from the US midterm elections.

US authorities have conducted a pre-dawn raid on the Washington-area home of Democratic US representative Ilhan Omar of Minnesota, an outspoken critic of Donald Trump who has been the target of political insults by the Republican president.

A person familiar with the investigation said it was related to alleged immigration fraud, and part of the probe concerned the Somali-born politician's immigration paperwork, which was filled out by her late father when she was a child.

"Today in the Washington, DC area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorised search warrant secured by the Department of Justice. This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal investigation," a Justice Department spokesperson said in an email.

Homeland Security Investigations is part of US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

Speaking outside a US military air base, Donald Trump told reporters officials were looking "very carefully" into Ms Omarr after the raid.

"I've always known her to be totally crooked", he said.

He said the congresswoman was a "complainer" from a "non-country" before departing for Ohio, where he will host a rally.

Agents of Homeland Security Investigations were seen in front of Ilhan Omar's home on Monday morning, US time. (Reuters: Annabelle Gordon)

Ms Omar called the search an "attempt to target political enemies and weaponise federal law enforcement".

Tom Homan, the Trump administration's "border tsar", told Fox Business Network the Justice Department was leading the investigation with the Department of Homeland Security.

Mr Homan declined to discuss the specifics of an ongoing criminal investigation.

The raid was carried out a little more than three weeks before the November 3 midterm elections, when Mr Trump's party will be trying to defend its narrow majorities in the US Congress.

Ms Omar, a prominent progressive who is running for re-election, represents a safe Democratic district.

She won re-election in 2024 by a margin of 50 percentage points.

Ilhan Omar has previously described Donald Trump's continuous criticism of her as "creepy". (Reuters: Nathan Howard)

Minnesota Democrats condemned the raid.

"Americans see this for what it is," Minnesota Governor Tim Walz, a Democrat, wrote on social media.

"President Trump is abusing his power to go after political opponents weeks before an election."

Justice Department policy bars federal prosecutors and agents from timing any action to affect the outcome of any election or benefiting a candidate or political party.

The department has historically avoided taking investigative steps against political candidates within about 60 days of an election.

Ms Omar has faced political insults from Mr Trump, who has cast the Somali American community as a threat to Minnesota in a burst of anti-Somali and anti-Muslim rhetoric.

She previously called Mr Trump's focus on her an "unhealthy and creepy obsession".

Last week, Mr Trump called Michigan's Democratic nominee for the US Senate — Abdul El-Sayed, who is ⁠Muslim — a "RADICAL Extremist" and "Terrorist Sympathizer" while offering support for Mr El-Sayed's Republican opponent, Mike Rogers.

Civil rights advocates have criticised Mr Trump's rhetoric toward minorities and immigrants, including when he previously called Somalis "garbage."

Mr Trump in February said Ms Omar and Democratic Representative Rashida Tlaib of Michigan, who is also Muslim, should be "institutionalised" and sent back to "where they came from".

Both congresswomen had criticised Mr Trump during his State of the Union address as he touted his administration's hardline immigration crackdown and its immigration enforcement actions.

Ms Omar has said she and her family have faced death threats, which she attributes to "hateful political rhetoric", especially from Mr Trump.

Last month, a Minnesota man who squirted vinegar on Ms Omar was sentenced to one year and two months in prison after pleading guilty to assaulting a federal official.

Anthony James Kazmierczak admitted to attacking Ms Omar because he disagreed with her progressive political views.

Reuters

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Federal agents raid Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar’s home weeks before Election Day, despite DOJ rules against political interference

DOJ’s rules caution prosecutors and agents against taking actions that could affect an election — or even create the perception that they are doing so.

Actual Article Body:
By Yunior Rivas

October 12, 2026

to see more of our voting rights news coverage when you search.

Federal agents raided Rep. Ilhan Omar’s Washington-area home Monday, just 22 days before the Minnesota Democrat faces reelection. The extraordinary move against a sitting member of Congress drew scrutiny over the Trump administration’s departure from longstanding Department of Justice (DOJ) guidance meant to prevent federal law enforcement from influencing elections.

Homeland Security Investigations, the investigative arm of ICE, carried out the search pursuant to a warrant obtained by the DOJ.

The investigation reportedly concerns Omar’s immigration history, including allegations of fraud that she has repeatedly denied. DOJ has not publicly detailed the evidence underlying the investigation or disclosed why agents executed the search so close to the election.

DOJ said only that the action was part of an “ongoing federal criminal investigation.”

Join 350,000 readers who rely on our daily and weekly newsletters for the latest in voting, elections and democracy.

The timing is especially notable because DOJ’s own rules caution prosecutors and agents against taking actions that could affect an election — or even create the perception that they are doing so.

The Justice Manual states that federal prosecutors and agents “may never select the timing” of investigative steps, charges or public statements for the purpose of affecting an election or giving an advantage or disadvantage to a candidate or political party. Any action likely to raise even the perception of such interference requires consultation with DOJ’s Public Integrity Section.

Separate DOJ rules require Public Integrity Section consultation in all investigations involving members of Congress, including before obtaining a search warrant for property belonging to a lawmaker. DOJ also requires urgent reports to department leadership for investigations involving declared candidates for federal office.

It is not yet clear whether those procedures were followed before agents searched Omar’s home.

“The Trump DOJ tears up yet another long-standing policy/norm, this one of refusing to take actions like this before an election,” immigration policy expert Aaron Reichlin-Melnick wrote following reports of the raid. “The DOJ today, after not even two years of Trump, is a rotten shell of what it once was; untrusted by sizeable portions of the federal judiciary, hollowed out at the core, and run without principle.”

DOJ did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The existence of a judicially authorized warrant means a judge found probable cause sufficient to permit the search. But the warrant itself does not resolve the separate question of why DOJ chose to execute such an overt law-enforcement action against a candidate less than a month before Election Day.

The Justice Department has long treated that distinction as significant. Further election-year guidance dating back to at least 2008 has emphasized that “politics must play no role” in investigative or charging decisions and that prosecutors should exercise particular caution around overt investigative steps close to elections. Similar guidance was subsequently issued across administrations.

Omar, who is seeking reelection to Minnesota’s 5th Congressional District, accused the administration of using federal law enforcement against a political opponent.

“Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement,” Omar wrote in response. “For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced.”

The search comes after months of public statements by senior Trump administration officials about investigating Omar.

Vice President JD Vance previously accused Omar of immigration fraud without providing evidence and said publicly that he and other administration officials were discussing how to investigate her and “build the case necessary” to pursue her.

President Donald Trump has also repeatedly singled out Omar, a Somali-born Muslim who became a U.S. citizen and was elected to Congress in 2018. As recently as this weekend, Trump attacked Omar at a rally and suggested that Vance and administration officials were investigating her.

Those attacks have unfolded alongside Trump’s broader bursts of anti-Somali and anti-Muslim rhetoric.

Democratic officials immediately blasted the timing of Monday’s search.

Democratic National Committee Chair Ken Martin called it “a new low for the Trump administration,” pointing specifically to the decision to search “the home of a U.S. congresswoman weeks out from Election Day.”

California Gov. Gavin Newsom (D) similarly highlighted the timing, writing: “Twenty-two days away from the midterm election, another politicized ‘investigation.’ Straight out of the authoritarian playbook.”

House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, Democratic Whip Katherine Clark and Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar also condemned the search, calling it “deeply disturbing” and saying it raised “serious questions” about what they described as the Trump administration’s weaponization of the federal government against political adversaries.

The Democratic leaders pointed to Trump’s years of attacks on Omar and emphasized the timing of the search less than a month before the midterms.

“Now, less than 30 days until the midterm election, his violent mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected Member of Congress and her family,” they said.

They also vowed congressional scrutiny, saying the public deserved transparency and promising “full accountability” for what they called an abuse of power by the Department of Homeland Security and DOJ.

The Trump administration continued airing taxpayer-funded ads promoting President Donald Trump after a federal judge ordered the campaign halted, then told the court that an internal email delay was to blame.
